oneLine: Controls the automated storage rack: one job per aisle at a time over PLC messages, placing every container and publishing the facts the flow upstairs needs.

rows.title: Request a store into the rack
rows.story: The warehouse control system asks to store the container waiting on an input port. The aisle's rack map picks and reserves a place at once - front for fast movers, back for slow - and refuses a container that is already in or already busy.

rows.title: Request a retrieve from the rack
rows.story: The warehouse control system names a stored container and an output port. An unknown container, or one already on its way, is refused; otherwise the job waits in its aisle's queue.

rows.title: Give the aisle its next job
rows.story: One job at a time per aisle. When the equipment finishes, the next store or retrieve is sent to it; when a front container blocks the one needed, an invisible shuffle clears the way first.
rows.policy: Whenever a job ends or a new one is accepted, the aisle's unit takes one next job

then.does: receives one job at a time and moves the container

rows.title: The equipment finishes a store
rows.story: The equipment answers that the motion is done. The container now sits in its reserved place, the finished-job answer is acknowledged so it never repeats, and the fact is published for the material flow system designed to read it.
rows.policy: Whenever the equipment reports a finished motion, record it and acknowledge the answer

rows.title: The container arrives at the port
rows.story: A retrieved container reaches its output port in request order. What the port read is recorded - a clean read, a no-read or a mismatch - and the presentation is published so someone can come and take it.
rows.policy: Whenever a container arrives at an output port, present the oldest retrieve waiting for it

rows.title: The equipment cannot run a job
rows.story: The equipment answers that a job cannot run: the container was not where the rack map said, the port was busy, or a fault. Each bare code becomes a plain failure reason and the job ends.
rows.policy: Whenever the equipment fails a job, end it with the mapped reason

rows.title: An aisle unit stops
rows.story: The equipment reports each aisle unit's state. A unit that changed state is published; a held unit fails every job still waiting in its aisle with an equipment fault and takes no new work until it clears.
rows.policy: Whenever a unit reports a new state, publish it; a held aisle loses its queued jobs

rows.title: Cancel a job
rows.story: The warehouse control system cancels a job. One still waiting is simply dropped; one already with the equipment asks it to stop, and its answer decides the outcome.

then.does: is asked to stop the job it holds, and answers

rows.title: The equipment answers a stop request
rows.story: An accepted stop ends the job as cancelled and frees what it held. A refused or never-answered stop lets the job run on, back to where it was before the request.
rows.policy: Whenever the equipment answers a stop request, end the job or let it go on

rows.title: Give up on silent equipment
rows.story: A command the equipment never acknowledges is resent three times, then its job fails as unreachable. A stop request that stays unanswered is called off, so the aisle is never left waiting on nothing.
rows.policy: After three unanswered retries, a command fails its job; an unanswered stop is called off

rows.title: Recover after a restart
rows.story: After a restart, every command the equipment never acknowledged is resent unchanged, pending stops too, and every aisle unit is asked to report its state before the aisles carry on.
rows.policy: At boot, resend everything unanswered and ask every unit its state

rows.title: Confirm the container was taken
rows.story: No message from the equipment ever says a container left an output port, so the taker confirms the pickup. The port becomes free and the next retrieve can be presented on it.

rows.title: Publish what the AS/RS can do
rows.story: Every change renews the whole system's numbers - units available, free places, open jobs - and the new capacity is published for the flow control designed to read it.
rows.policy: Whenever an aisle's numbers move, publish the AS/RS's capacity

rows.title: Let an agent look, not touch
rows.story: A read-only agent surface answers where a job stands, what waits on each port and how full the system is - without touching the material flow. Nothing can be changed from it.

hotspots.text: A finished-job answer lost while the service was down leaves the job stuck as acknowledged; protocol v1 has no way to ask the equipment what became of it.
A stop the equipment accepted whose answer (and its retries) are all lost leaves the job waiting forever: the aisle stays busy and the place stays reserved.
When the rack disagrees with the stored map, the job fails as a mismatch but the offending position is not blocked, so the next job can hit it again.
No fleet context consumes the five published facts yet: the material flow system meant to read them, and fault cases for equipment faults, are designed, not built.
A retrieve to a port whose earlier pickup was never confirmed replaces the container still waiting on it; the overlap is only logged.

opportunities.text: The analytics twin of every fact has no reader yet; it is kept as the fleet's analytics data slot.
